### why it can't be represented exactly
in binary floating-point systems (like ieee 754), numbers are stored with a finite number of bits. decimal 0.1 is **1/10**, and 10 has prime factors 2 and 5. binary can only represent fractions with denominators that are powers of 2 (like 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, etc.). since 10 is not a power of 2, 1/10 cannot be expressed as a finite sum of negative powers of 2. this causes an infinite, repeating binary fraction, which must be truncated or rounded when stored in finite bits. hence, **0.1 cannot be represented exactly in binary floating-point.**
